biergerpakt.title: What is the Biergerpakt?
biergerpakt.text: The Biergerpakt (Citizens' Pact) is a government programme designed to foster intercultural living-together in Luxembourg. It connects newcomers and long-term residents through activities, events, and shared experiences — helping everyone feel at home.

languages.title: Luxembourg's languages
languages.text: Luxembourg has three official languages: Luxembourgish, French, and German. Luxembourgish (Lëtzebuergesch) is the national language and a symbol of cultural identity. Many residents also speak English and Portuguese.

intercultural.title: Intercultural living-together
intercultural.text: Nearly half of Luxembourg's residents are foreign nationals. This rich diversity is one of Luxembourg's greatest strengths. Living and working together across cultures requires understanding, respect, and curiosity — exactly what these activities are designed to encourage.
intercultural.heading: Intercultural Activities
intercultural.subheading: Ideas for connecting across cultures — in your neighbourhood, at work, and in everyday life in Luxembourg.

lang-moien.title: Say "Moien" to three people
lang-moien.tip: "Moien" (MOY-en) is the most common Luxembourgish greeting, used any time of day. Try it with a shopkeeper, neighbour, or colleague. A smile goes a long way!

explore-walk.title: Take a walk in a new neighbourhood
explore-walk.tip: Explore a part of Luxembourg you've never visited — a different commune, a new street, or a park. Try Bonnevoie, Hollerich, Esch-sur-Alzette, or Differdange.

culture-song.title: Listen to a Luxembourgish song
culture-song.tip: Find and listen to a song in Lëtzebuergesch. Try artists like Serge Tonnar, Def Dogg, or look up "Ons Heemecht" — the national anthem. Search "musique lëtzebuergesch" or browse the RTL Lëtzebuerg music playlist.

lang-5phrases.title: Learn 5 everyday Luxembourgish phrases
lang-5phrases.tip: Master these: "Moien" (hello), "Äddi" (goodbye), "Merci" (thank you), "Wéi geet et?" (how are you?), "Ech verstinn net" (I don't understand). Write them on a sticky note!

culture-dish.title: Try a traditional Luxembourgish dish
culture-dish.tip: Try Judd mat Gaardebounen (smoked pork with broad beans), Bouneschlupp (green bean soup), or Gromperekichelcher (potato fritters) at a local restaurant.

lang-french-cafe.title: Order something in French at a café
lang-french-cafe.tip: "Un café, s'il vous plaît" (a coffee, please). "L'addition, s'il vous plaît" means "the bill, please". French is one of Luxembourg's three official languages!

lang-nature.title: Learn 5 nature words in Luxembourgish
lang-nature.tip: Learn: Bësch (forest), Floss (river), Bierg (mountain/hill), Blumm (flower), Vull (bird). Try naming what you see on a walk — it makes vocabulary stick!

lang-hello-neighbor.title: Learn to say "hello" in a neighbour's language
lang-hello-neighbor.tip: Find out what language your neighbour, colleague, or friend speaks at home, then learn their greeting. Luxembourg has residents from over 170 nationalities!

explore-park.title: Spend an hour in a Luxembourg park
explore-park.tip: Try Parc de Merl, Parc Schlassbësch, or the gardens of the Abbaye de Neumünster in the Grund. Observe the people around you — Luxembourg's parks reflect the country's remarkable diversity.

explore-train.title: Take a train to a town you've never visited
explore-train.tip: Luxembourg's public transport (trains, buses, trams) is completely free! Use it to visit a town or village you've never been to. Luxembourg was the first country in the world to make all public transport free (2020).

culture-tradition.title: Read about a Luxembourg tradition
culture-tradition.tip: Look up one Luxembourg cultural tradition: the Schueberfouer fair, Émaischen (pottery fair), the Octave pilgrimage, Bretzelsonndeg (Pretzel Sunday), or the Dancing Procession of Echternach.

culture-event.title: Attend a free cultural event
culture-event.tip: Attend an outdoor concert, art exhibition opening, street performance, or public lecture. Check the Agenda Culturel (agenda.lu) for free events near you.

connect-coffee.title: Have coffee with someone from a different culture
connect-coffee.tip: Invite a colleague, classmate, or acquaintance from a different cultural background for a coffee or tea. Ask them one thing they love about their home country. Be curious — everyone has a fascinating story.

explore-museum.title: Visit a local museum or cultural site
explore-museum.tip: Spend at least 30 minutes at a museum, castle, or cultural heritage site. Options include MUDAM, Musée National, Casino Luxembourg, Vianden Castle, or any of the many maisons de la culture.

culture-film.title: Watch a film from a different culture
culture-film.tip: Watch a film or documentary from a culture different from your own — bonus if it's from one of Luxembourg's many represented nationalities. Cinémathèque de la Ville de Luxembourg shows international films regularly.

biergerpakt-register.title: Register on the Biergerpakt platform
biergerpakt-register.tip: Create your account on biergerpakt.zesummeliewen.lu. Explore the activities and events available in your area. Registration is free and available in multiple languages.

connect-neighbour.title: Ask a neighbour where they're from
connect-neighbour.tip: Strike up a conversation with a neighbour you don't know well. Ask where they're originally from and share where you're from too. A simple "Hi, I don't think we've properly met yet" works perfectly.

lang-directions.title: Use Luxembourgish to ask for directions
lang-directions.tip: "Wou ass...?" means "Where is...?". "Kënnt Dir mir soen, wou... ass?" = "Could you tell me where... is?" is even more polite.

lang-news.title: Read a news article in a language you're learning
lang-news.tip: Try RTL.lu for Luxembourgish, Tageblatt.lu for French, or Wort.lu for German. Even reading headlines and captions counts — the habit is what matters!

explore-market.title: Visit a local weekly market
explore-market.tip: Head to one of Luxembourg's weekly markets — such as the Marché de la Ville in Luxembourg City. Buy at least one item and chat briefly with a vendor.

explore-nature.title: Explore a natural site in Luxembourg
explore-nature.tip: Visit the Müllerthal (Little Switzerland), the Moselle Valley, the Ardennes, or the Minett Biosphere Reserve. Visit Luxembourg (visitluxembourg.com) has excellent trail maps.

explore-institution.title: Visit a public institution
explore-institution.tip: Visit the Chamber of Deputies (guided tours available at chd.lu), the European Court of Justice, or a local town hall (mairie). The Luxembourg Parliament offers free guided tours.

connect-meal.title: Share a meal from your own culture
connect-meal.tip: Cook or share a dish from your own cultural background with a colleague, friend, or neighbour. Use food as a bridge to tell them something about where you're from.

connect-sport.title: Join a group sport or fitness activity
connect-sport.tip: Participate in a group sport or fitness session — a running club, yoga class, football match, or group hike. Sport is a universal language that breaks barriers.

connect-language-exchange.title: Join a language exchange
connect-language-exchange.tip: Find a partner who wants to learn your language while you learn theirs. Meet for 30 minutes, switching halfway. Language exchanges can be found through Biergerpakt, Meetup.com, or local Facebook groups.

culture-industrial.title: Explore Luxembourg's industrial heritage
culture-industrial.tip: Visit the former blast furnaces at Belval (Esch-sur-Alzette), the National Mining Museum in Rumelange, or the Fond-de-Gras heritage railway site.

biergerpakt-module.title: Complete a Biergerpakt online module
biergerpakt-module.tip: Complete at least one short online course or module available through the Biergerpakt platform about Luxembourg's culture, institutions, or intercultural living.

connect-volunteer.title: Volunteer for a local community activity
connect-volunteer.tip: Sign up for a one-time volunteering activity — a clean-up day, a food bank, a community garden, or helping a local association. Search for opportunities on luxassoc.lu or your commune's website.

connect-gathering.title: Organise a neighbourhood gathering
connect-gathering.tip: Take the initiative: organise a small gathering — a picnic, board game night, or barbecue — and invite people from at least two different cultural backgrounds. You can get inspiration and support through the Biergerpakt platform.

biergerpakt-attend.title: Attend a Biergerpakt event
biergerpakt-attend.tip: Sign up for and attend a Biergerpakt event or activity in your area — a guided walk, cooking class, language exchange, or community gathering. Browse activities sorted by your commune.

biergerpakt-invite.title: Invite someone to a Biergerpakt event
biergerpakt-invite.tip: Find a Biergerpakt event you find interesting, then invite a friend, neighbour, or colleague to join you. Sharing the experience makes it even richer.

biergerpakt-organise.title: Organise a Biergerpakt-inspired gathering
biergerpakt-organise.tip: Take the initiative: organise a small gathering and invite people from at least two different cultural backgrounds. You can get inspiration and even support for your event through the Biergerpakt platform.
